 Thanksgiving travel at SEA airport: TSA shares security tips, food rules, and craziest items found in carry-on
 Nov 20, 2026, 11:20 AM
 Travelers pass through TSA at SEA airport. (Photo courtesy of the Port of Seattle)
 (Photo courtesy of the Port of Seattle)
 BY LUKE DUECY 
 KIRO Newsradio Reporter
 Thanksgiving travel is getting underway, and the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) is preparing for a busy week at the Seattle-Tacoma International Airport (SEA).
 TSA expects passenger numbers to start climbing Friday, with the busiest days at SEA expected to be Tuesday and Wednesday before Thanksgiving.
 Nationwide, the Sunday after Thanksgiving is expected to be the busiest travel day, with TSA potentially screening 3 million or more passengers.
 Jessica Mayle, a regional TSA spokesperson, said travelers can avoid unnecessary delays by arriving early, checking their identification, and packing carefully.
 How early should you arrive at SEA?
 TSA recommends arriving at the airport at least two hours before your flight.
 “We really just want passengers to be prepared, arriving early, give yourself plenty of time,” TSA spokesperson Jessica Mayle explained. “Those rush hour time periods, usually in the morning, 5 a.m. to 8 a.m. And there’s usually an afternoon rush hour as well. We recommend two hours. That’s two hours from when you step foot in the airport. So, if you’re dropping off a rental car, parking, give yourself a bit of extra time for that.”
 Mayle said arriving early can make the difference when something goes wrong.
 A forgotten pocketknife, oversized bottle of shampoo, or other prohibited item is much easier to deal with when you aren’t racing to catch a flight.
 TSA warns travelers about REAL ID requirements
 Travelers should check their identification before heading to the airport.
 A REAL ID-compliant driver’s license or passport is an acceptable form of identification.
 Passengers without an acceptable ID can use TSA Confirm.ID , an identity verification system that requires an online process and a $45 fee.
 Travelers must complete that process before arriving at the airport and bring a printed or digital copy of their receipt.
 If they wait until reaching the security checkpoint, they could be sent out of line to complete the process, adding more time to their trip.
 TSA recommends checking its official list of acceptable identification.
 TSA PreCheck Touchless ID can speed up screening
 Eligible TSA PreCheck passengers may also be able to use Touchless ID at participating checkpoints.
 The system uses facial verification instead of requiring passengers to present their identification at the checkpoint.
 However, travelers must opt in ahead of time through their airline profile, upload a passport photo, and have a Known Traveler Number associated with their PreCheck membership.
 An indicator on the boarding pass lets TSA officers know the passenger is eligible.
 Mayle said it’s a faster option within the PreCheck experience, but travelers cannot simply sign up when they arrive at the airport.
 Thanksgiving food: What can you bring through security?
 Thanksgiving leftovers can create confusion at airport security, particularly when it comes to the difference between solid foods and liquids.
 “Solid foods like turkey stuffing, cakes, pies, cookies — those are good in any quantity in your checked or carry-on bags,” Mayle said. “When you’re looking at those soft, spreadable liquid foods, so mashed potatoes, cranberry sauce, gravy, wine, anything like that, that’s going to need to be 3.4 ounces or less to go in your carry-on bag. Anything bigger than that needs to go in your checked bag.”
 The less you bring through, the quicker you’re going to get scanned.
 Travelers can check individual items using TSA’s online What Can I Bring search tool .
 SEA travelers can choose between security checkpoints
 One advantage at SEA is that all security checkpoints provide access to all gates.
 That gives passengers some flexibility to choose the checkpoint with the shortest wait.
 Mayle said TSA works with the airport and airlines to project passenger volume by the hour and adjust staffing and security lanes accordingly.
 Travelers should also monitor their airline’s app for schedule changes, cancellations, and weather-related disruptions that could affect passenger volume.
 TSA highlights unusual items found in luggage
 And if you’re wondering what people actually try to bring through airport security, TSA said the unusual discoveries never stop.
 Agents showed KIRO Newsradio hundreds of items they discovered inside passengers’ carry-on luggage over just a few days from just one security line, including knives, pruning shears, an unloaded handgun magazine, a blow torch, scissors, and more.
 Mayle pointed to a recent example involving oversized metal Wolverine claws that were prohibited from going through security.
 Wolverine claw found at SEA Airport. (Photo courtesy of the Transportation Security Administration)
 TSA also recently highlighted an incident in California involving live snakes found inside checked luggage.
 “We just had a story out of California in the last week that was live snakes someone put in their checked baggage. So there really is no limit to what passengers will either intentionally or accidentally bring through,” she said. “Take a beat, think about what you’re putting in your bag. But I also hope reassuring passengers that TSA officers are very well trained to spot these things, and these items are not making it onto the aircraft, because safety is our top priority.”
 Her biggest advice for Thanksgiving travelers is to pack smart, arrive early and be patient.

 SEA Spot Saver and parking during holidays
 SEA spokesperson Perry Cooper said the airport’s Spot Saver program , which allows passengers to save a spot in a TSA security line, will be up and running through the Thanksgiving holiday, but will then sunset.
 “It’s going to be still in operation through Nov. 29, and then on Nov. 30 it will go away,” Cooper explained. “The reason for that is because we’ve done so much better with our expansion for our checkpoints. We’ve got a new, updated checkpoint six where we’ve added new lanes, a brand-new checkpoint, and checkpoint one on the south end. So, we are seeing our wait times have dived down to the point where 94% of our passengers get through the checkpoints in 20 minutes or less.”
 SEA is offering 600 extra parking spots for passengers to reserve in advance.
 “Do that ahead of time. I suggest doing it at least seven days in advance because once they fill up, you don’t get any more opportunity to get into reserved parking,” Cooper said.
 And, for the holiday period, SEA is offering a 90-minute grace period in general parking for people dropping off and picking up passengers. Between their busiest hours, 7 p.m. to midnight, people can park for free and go inside their terminal to pick up passengers.
